focus: correctness — the packet-log lock after the workspace-root rewiring

findingDetails.title: The packet-log lock's root escapes the documented state-dir override, so an isolated probe still creates directories in the repository's real .state/goal tree
findingDetails.evidence: appendPacketLog locks packetLockRoot(root) (goal-core.cjs:1070), which is join(workspace, STATE_SUBDIR) (goal-core.cjs:902-904, STATE_SUBDIR '.opencode/skills/.state/goal' at :45), not the resolved session state directory; acquireFileLock mkdirs that tree recursively on every acquisition (:540-543). The README's override row calls OPENCODE_GOAL_STATE_DIR the device that lets tests and isolated probes avoid touching the real .state/goal tree (README.md:130), while the state row correctly says packet-log locks live under the workspace's default state root (README.md:143). Reproduced with the shipped CLI on a fixture workspace under this lineage: with both sessions rerouted to scratch/state-a and scratch/state-b, 40 of 40 concurrent log rows landed (pass-2 F101 fixed) and LOCK_TREE_UNDER_WORKSPACE=true — <workspace>/.opencode/skills/.state/goal/.locks/ was created despite both overrides; the lock directory itself is removed on release (:578-582), the .locks parent remains. An alias workspace symlinked to the same tree landed 20 of 20 rows against the real-path session (real-path key at :898-900 via goal-slice.cjs:188-200).
findingDetails.impact: A test or probe that trusts the documented override to leave the repository state tree untouched now leaves an empty gitignored .locks/ directory inside it. The serialization requirement is the reason the root moved, so the design is right and the stale half of the README pair is the defect.
findingDetails.recommendation: State the precondition in the override row: the packet-log lock root always follows the workspace, so a probe against a real workspace still creates <workspace>/.opencode/skills/.state/goal/.locks/ and should pass a fixture workspace when that matters. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Lock acquisition, naming, state-dir resolution and the mkdir on acquisition read directly; the row count and the created lock tree reproduced end to end with the shipped CLI and a same-stack positive control for the pass-2 fix.

focus: correctness — the two frontmatter boundaries behind the goal slice

findingDetails.title: On an unclosed frontmatter fence the validator still measures the frontmatter as part of the durable slice where the runtime fails closed
findingDetails.evidence: The runtime's opener-only branch fails closed (goal-slice.cjs:42-45 returns body '' and readPacketGoal null at :255); the validator's copy has no branch and falls back to the whole document when the fence does not match (spec-doc-structure.ts:1030-1031: const body = fence ? normalized.slice(fence[0].length) : normalized). Both shipped modules executed over a ten-spelling matrix agreed on nine spellings (exact, trailing space, trailing tab, both, CR-only, CRLF, BOM+comment, no frontmatter, trailing newline: 164 vs 164 each) and diverged on the unclosed opener: runtime readPacketGoal null / extractDurableSlice 0 characters against validator extractGoalDurableSlice 4400 characters on a 4200-character body. Through the shipped rules the same fixture reports SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_005 error 'durable slice is 4400 characters (> 4000)' alongside SPECDOC_FRONTMATTER_001, so the document already fails and no false pass exists; the quoted budget number counts the frontmatter.
findingDetails.impact: A broken goal.md gets a budget diagnostic measured over the frontmatter, the one leak the shared module exists to prevent, and can carry a spurious over-budget error. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Give the validator's copy the runtime's opener-only branch, or scope ADR-003's agreement promise to closed fences. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both production modules executed on identical bytes across ten inputs; the rule runner executed on the divergent fixture; the runtime's fail-closed branch read at the cited lines.

findingDetails.title: The validator's strict frontmatter parser and its tolerant goal extractor disagree on the same document, so a trailing-space fence silently waives the continuity block goal.md is required to carry
findingDetails.evidence: The general parser normalizes CRLF only and demands exact fences (spec-doc-structure.ts:276-278), while the goal extractor normalizes bare CR and tolerates [ \t]* on both fences (:1029-1030). goal.md is deliberately not in OPTIONAL_CONTINUITY_DOCS (:212-213) so the memory-block rule requires its continuity block and reports SPECDOC_FRONTMATTER_002 when missing (:705-712), but it reaches that check only through the strict parser (:690) and continues silently when no frontmatter parses (:701-703). Reproduced through the shipped rule on three spellings of one document without a _memory block: exact fence -> status=warn with SPECDOC_FRONTMATTER_002 'goal.md: missing _memory block'; trailing-space fence -> status=pass with no diagnostics while SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY measures the same 164-character slice; no frontmatter at all -> status=pass.
findingDetails.impact: A goal.md whose fence carries a trailing space or tab escapes the continuity requirement an identical document must satisfy. Advisory in effect and unusual in trigger, but it is the same boundary drift pass-2 F102 named. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Use the shared boundary for both rules inside the validator, or record the asymmetry with a test that pins it. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Three rule executions over three document spellings with the shipped rule runner; both boundary regexes read at the cited lines; the document-set comment read at :212-213.

findingDetails.title: The phase-008 parity test asserts the validator agrees with itself, and ADR-003's promised golden pin against the continuity boundary still does not exist
findingDetails.evidence: The new case is named 'measures the same slice as the runtime extractor when a fence carries trailing whitespace or bare CR' but its three assertions compare extractGoalDurableSlice against itself (spec-doc-structure.vitest.ts:326-328); the suite imports only the validator module (:9-14) and never references .opencode/hooks/goal/lib/goal-slice.cjs. ADR-003 still promises a pin against continuity-freshness.ts:17 (decision-record.md:265), whose regex at continuity-freshness.ts:21 is a third variant. A repository-wide grep for extractGoalDurableSlice returns the module, its dist, the suite and this lineage's probes only.
findingDetails.impact: A future edit to either fence matcher leaves the suite green, which is the failure mode pass-2 F102 recorded; ADR-003's acceptance promise remains unmet after the phase whose purpose included closing it. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Import the runtime extractor in the vitest case and assert equality on the same fixtures, or replace the ADR's pin sentence with the boundary the project keeps. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The test reads its own module in all three assertions and imports nothing from the runtime; the ADR sentence and the continuity boundary regex read at the cited lines; the grep covered the repository excluding node_modules and worktrees.

focus: traceability — the plugin's shared append against its documentation, and the log rule's own condition

findingDetails.title: Three sentences in the hook README still say the OpenCode plugin imports only the slice module, while the plugin imports the core's locked append
findingDetails.evidence: The plugin requires the core (opencode-goal.js:26-27: const { appendPacketLog: appendPacketLogShared } = require('../hooks/goal/lib/goal-core.cjs')) and calls it in the log action (:3024). The README denies it at :29 ('the OpenCode plugin requires lib/goal-slice.cjs and nothing else from this tree'), :117 ('imports nothing else from this tree') and :140 ('The OpenCode plugin imports goal-slice.cjs only'), while the same file's State row at :143 records the shared lock and goal-plugin.md:34,42,113 records the shared append. The opencode/ path is a real symlink (git ls-files -s mode 120000), so there is no second copy to drift.
findingDetails.impact: The component README states the two implementations cannot share a write path, which is exactly the property phase 008 changed to make the packet lock meaningful. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Fold the shared append into the three sentences: the plugin imports and calls goal-core.cjs's appendPacketLog and nothing else. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Require block, call site, the three README sentences, the sibling document's three statements and the symlink mode all read directly.

findingDetails.title: The narrowed log rule permits a direct row append for a packet no session is bound to, a condition no shipped surface can answer
findingDetails.evidence: The rule (speckit-plan.yaml:200, speckit-implement.yaml:165, speckit-complete.yaml:258, save.md:61) permits a direct table-row append 'only for a packet no session is bound to'. The session-free read reports no bound-ness: describePacketGoal returns exactly packetPath, nested, durableChars, budgetState, hash, chatSlice, objectiveSlice (goal-core.cjs:998-1006) and the CLI packet action prints the same set (bin/goal.cjs:211-219). Every other read is per-session or aggregate: show needs the session's own record (bin/goal.cjs:139-143), history lists archives (:273-291), doctor/health return counts (:293-307). A bind exists only as packetPath inside one opaque per-session record (goal-core.cjs:950-965). Cursor exposes only the session-free packet read (.cursor/commands/goal-cursor.md:2-3,46) and Devin has no command surface, so the runtimes that must always take the carve-out cannot evaluate it.
findingDetails.impact: The qualifier pass-2 F104 introduced is not decidable from any surface, so 'never append directly' and 'append when nothing is bound' cannot be told apart by the agent the rule addresses; on the two injection-only runtimes it degrades to an unpinned unlocked append, the original exposure narrowed in prose only. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Either add a packet_bound field to the session-free read (a bounded scan of active records for that packetPath), or drop the carve-out and state that tooling appends only through the log action. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The rule text read in all four contracts; the complete field set of the session-free read taken from the core function and from a live CLI invocation; every other read surface's scope read at the cited lines.

findingDetails.title: The README says the session-free packet read needs only --workspace; the CLI refuses it without a session identity
findingDetails.evidence: README.md:62 states that packet 'needs only --workspace', and README.md:60 and goal-plugin.md:42 call it a session-free read. The router disagrees: bin/goal.cjs:386-393 runs core.resolveGoalScope for every action except doctor, health, legacy-inspect and legacy-archive, and resolveGoalScope throws MISSING_SESSION_ID before any handler (goal-core.cjs:180-183). Reproduced with the shipped CLI over the iteration-1 fixture: 'packet <fixture> --workspace <ws>' -> STATUS=FAIL ACTION=packet ERROR="Session identity is required" code=MISSING_SESSION_ID; adding --runtime alone still MISSING_SESSION_ID; with --runtime cursortest --session cmd --workspace <ws> -> STATUS=OK ACTION=packet with all seven fields. runPacket itself reads only options.scope.workspace (bin/goal.cjs:206-219), and the shipped Cursor command works around the pre-check by passing a placeholder scope (.cursor/commands/goal-cursor.md:27).
findingDetails.impact: The one action documented as needing no session is the one whose documented invocation fails, pushing the operator to invent an identity for a read that never uses it. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add packet to actionsWithoutScope in the router so the documented invocation works and the Cursor command can drop its placeholder scope. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Three live CLI invocations with different scope flag sets over one fixture; the pre-check, the action handler and the identity requirement read at the cited lines.

focus: security — the log row as an input surface, and rebind history across the two implementations

findingDetails.title: A log row carrying anchor markup passes the sanitizer and makes the packet fail the sufficiency rule it previously passed
findingDetails.evidence: appendPacketLog sanitizes the row with sanitizeInlineText(item, 200) (goal-core.cjs:1063), whose pipeline collapses newlines and folds role tokens and [active_goal] markers but never neutralizes anchor markup (goal-core.cjs:255-278). The validator's anchor parser treats a second opener for an id already on the stack as a hard error (spec-doc-structure.ts:599-603) and turns any parse error into SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_001 at severity error (:1089-1097); unlike the orchestrator's whole-line anchor integrity check (orchestrator.ts:689-706) this parser matches anchor syntax inside a table row (:596-597). Reproduced with the shipped CLI and rule runner: a clean fixture passes SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY with no diagnostics; one log invocation with the item 'documented the <!-- ANCHOR:log --> section' returns STATUS=OK ACTION=log mutation=logged and writes the row verbatim; the same rule then reports status=fail with 'line 26: nested anchor 'log' is not legal', 'line 21: unclosed anchor 'log'' and 'goal.md:log is empty' while the durable slice stays byte-identical to the clean fixture and the append guard never fires.
findingDetails.impact: The sanctioned write path can invalidate the packet's own validation from an ordinary-looking log note. The append is not a privilege boundary, so this is a robustness defect in sanitizer coverage, and it fails loudly rather than silently. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Neutralize anchor markup in the inline sanitizer the way [active_goal] markers and fences already are, or escape < and > before inserting a row. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: End-to-end through the shipped CLI into a fixture under this lineage, then the shipped rule runner on the same folder before and after; the parser and rule turn parse errors into errors read at the cited lines.

findingDetails.title: A rebind archives the prior record in the core but overwrites it in place in the OpenCode plugin, so the two implementations keep different history
findingDetails.evidence: The core archives before writing the new record (goal-core.cjs:945-949 calls archiveGoalRecord when the packet path changes or the current record is terminal; the archive write is keyed on the record digest at :661-671). The plugin's bindGoal builds the next record and hands it to mutateGoal, which reads, mutates and writes the single file in place (opencode-goal.js:1818-1855, :1691-1700) with no archive step; archiveGoalStateFile is called only from the stale-session sweep (:1541) and session.deleted (:3229). Reproduced through the shipped CLI on the iteration-4 fixture: bind specs/t/001-alpha then bind specs/t/002-beta reports mutation=rebound and leaves history at archive_count=1 with archived packetPath 'specs/t/001-alpha'. The plugin half is read at every archive call site rather than exercised through its harness.
findingDetails.impact: On OpenCode the prior packet pointer and the operator copy derived from it are replaced with no history entry, while the same action on Pi, Cursor and Devin keeps the record; the phase-008 summary reports the guard as built without scoping it to the core. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Archive in the plugin's bind when the packet path changes, or state that rebind archiving is core-only. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Core archive path reproduced end to end with the shipped CLI and its history output; the plugin's absence established from the complete archive call-site list plus mutateGoal's read-modify-write.

focus: traceability — the review target's own claims, and the two deferred rows

findingDetails.title: The recorded Devin limitation names two same-field emitters where the shipped chain has three, so the live check it defers to is scoped to the wrong chain
findingDetails.evidence: The recorded limitation reads 'two UserPromptSubmit hooks write additionalContext; which one the host keeps is unrecorded until DV-022 runs live' (008-hardening-research/implementation-summary.md:119). The shipped chain has three entries for that event: .devin/hooks.v1.json UserPromptSubmit[0].hooks lists dist/hooks/devin/user-prompt-submit.js (:45), then runtime/hooks/devin/spec-gate-classify.mjs (:50), then .opencode/hooks/goal/devin/goal-inject.mjs (:55). All three reach the same field: the first normalizes a Claude-shaped hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext and re-emits it (runtime/dist/hooks/devin/shared.js:95-108 -> :84-93), the gate shim writes it directly (runtime/hooks/devin/spec-gate-classify.mjs:21), and the goal adapter writes the brief plus the resend reminder into it (.opencode/hooks/goal/devin/goal-inject.mjs:78). On a turn where a packet goal is active and the gate has a question, two of them emit a non-empty value in the same event; the shared shim emits whenever it has context of its own.
findingDetails.impact: Whoever runs DV-022 to settle the merge question would test a two-writer chain and conclude from it; a host rule that keeps the last writer would silently drop the spec-gate question and one that keeps the first would drop the goal brief — the failure modes the check exists to find, on a chain the note describes incompletely. P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Restate the limitation as 'three UserPromptSubmit entries can write hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (the shared shim, the gate question, the goal brief); the host's merge rule is unrecorded', and have DV-022 assert all three. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The three entries enumerated from .devin/hooks.v1.json UserPromptSubmit[0].hooks; each emitter's write path read at the cited lines; DV-022's step text read in the 007 packet. No command was run — the merge rule is host behavior.

results.summary: ADR-003's promised golden pin is still absent and the validator's two frontmatter boundaries disagree; every other frozen decision checked is implemented.
Every task and success criterion holds against disk state and the parent goal log.
The target is a spec folder, not a skill-agent pair.
Pi, Cursor and Devin inherit the core's rebind archive; the OpenCode plugin overwrites the prior record in place.
goal-plugin.md is current; the hook README still denies the plugin's second import and the plugins README omits unbind/log.
The log carve-out is undecidable, the packet example fails as written, and the recorded Devin chain undercounts its writers.
